speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you were brought in for bizarre and agitated behavior; to help me understand what is happening, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if he has had any recent head injuries or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, paranoid type.

The patient presents with a 6-week history of persecutory delusions (being spied on/controlled by NSA), bizarre behavior, and social withdrawal leading to job termination. Given the duration and severity of these psychotic symptoms, along with the duration of prodromal depressive symptoms, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of schizophrenia. No further questions or tests are required at this time.
